title: Faith and a fresh start
subtitle: Day 0-1
description: The first day or two is about protecting what just happened. Keep your faith close, stay calm, make Ghusl, and pick one or two next steps you trust. You do not have to rebuild your whole life by tomorrow.
mainGoal: Know what your Shahada means, get through the first 24 hours gently, and make Ghusl when you feel ready.
success: You know you are Muslim, you have one simple next step, and you are not forcing yourself to learn all of it at once.
dontWorry: Long prayers can wait. Nobody expects you to have them memorized.
You do not have to change your name. It is not required.
You do not have to announce anything to anyone yet.
You will not know every rule for a long time, and that is how it goes for everyone.
focusNow: Hold on to what the Shahada means to you.
Make Ghusl when you have time to do it calmly.
Pick one person or one masjid you can contact.
canWait: Detailed rulings and the arguments around them.
Changing your name, your wardrobe, or your whole routine at once.
Explaining Islam to everyone you know.
askHelpIf: You do not feel safe telling your family.
You are not sure how to do Ghusl.
You need a witness, a certificate, or a way into a local community.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I talk to family?

title: Getting the basics in place
subtitle: Week 1
description: This week is for gentle practice. You learn the shape of prayer, visit or at least phone a masjid, and start using short remembrance. None of it has to be done perfectly.
mainGoal: Start praying in a way you can actually keep up, and make one first contact with other Muslims.
success: You are praying in some form and you know where to go locally when you need help.
dontWorry: Your Arabic pronunciation does not have to be right yet.
Missing prayers while you are still learning is normal.
Feeling out of place at the masjid the first few times is normal too.
Optional practices can wait until the required ones feel steady.
focusNow: Learn the prayer times and the basic movements.
Find one masjid or one mentor you can ask questions.
Use short dua and dhikr to keep your heart in it.
canWait: Optional prayers and the finer differences of opinion.
Learning every custom at every masjid.
askHelpIf: The basics of prayer still confuse you.
Walking into a masjid makes you nervous.
Work or school makes prayer times hard to hit.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I visit a masjid?
How do I build prayer slowly?

title: Settling into practice
subtitle: Weeks 2-4
description: Things are starting to settle. Now you add the Quran, work out what to say to family, and find a healthier way to handle the questions that come up without drowning in them.
mainGoal: Start a small Quran habit, get ready for the conversations with family and friends, and learn how to ask a question well.
success: You read or listen to some Quran regularly, you have a line or two ready for the people closest to you, and doubts do not knock you over the way they did.
dontWorry: Reading Arabic fluently is a long way off for almost everyone.
You will not understand every verse. Neither does anyone else on a first read.
Faith going up and down does not mean it is failing.
You do not have to win any arguments.
focusNow: Read or listen to a little Quran on a regular basis.
Decide who needs to know about your Islam, and when.
Take the hard questions to people who actually know.
canWait: Answering every family objection on the spot.
askHelpIf: Family pressure turns unsafe or controlling.
Doubts are stopping you from functioning.
You cannot tell which sources are reliable.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I protect family ties?

title: Islam in daily life
subtitle: Months 2-3
description: Here Islam works its way into ordinary days: what you eat, how you get ready for fasting, how you dress, and where you draw practical lines. Set the pace so you can keep it up.
mainGoal: Learn the halal basics, get ready for fasting, and treat modesty as something you grow into rather than something to panic about.
success: You can shop and order food without stress, you know how fasting works at a beginner level, and you can tell which lifestyle questions need a local answer.
dontWorry: Your whole pantry does not have to change overnight.
One unclear ingredient is not an emergency.
How fast someone else changed their clothing has nothing to do with you.
Random online comments are not the place to sort out questions about fasting and hardship.
focusNow: Steer clear of the clearly haram foods and get comfortable with simple halal choices.
Learn how fasting works before Ramadan or your first voluntary fast.
Change one thing at a time with clothing, and keep it sustainable.
askHelpIf: Pressure about food or clothing is putting your safety at home at risk.
A medical condition might affect fasting.
You need a ruling about work, school, or money.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I eat halal in practice?

title: Character and steady learning
subtitle: Months 4-6
description: The practice is starting to feel familiar. This stage is about character, learning from people worth learning from, and asking better questions so you keep growing without spinning out.
mainGoal: Work on your character, learn how to put a question to someone qualified, and settle on a steady way to keep learning.
success: You can see a difference in how you treat people day to day, and you know where your learning goes next without it swallowing you.
dontWorry: You are not trying to become a scholar.
You will not know every opinion on every question.
Questions still coming up is a sign you are paying attention.
Islam is not meant to run as constant self-criticism.
focusNow: Be honest, be patient, keep praying, and treat people well.
Learn how to put a personal question into clear words.
Pick one class, one teacher, or one book and stay with it.
canWait: Keeping up with every speaker online.
Having an answer ready for every controversial topic.
askHelpIf: You are getting conflicting answers and feel stuck.
A ruling affects your family, marriage, work, or money.
Something about your community feels pressuring or unhealthy.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I ask good questions?

title: Growth over a lifetime
subtitle: Beyond 6 months
description: Islam is a lifelong path. This stage looks at the bigger responsibilities ahead, zakat and Hajj, while keeping your learning at a pace you can hold.
mainGoal: Get a picture of the pillars still ahead of you and keep learning with people who are qualified to teach.
success: You know zakat and Hajj become real obligations once the conditions apply to you, and you know to have your own situation checked by someone qualified.
dontWorry: Hajj is not owed until you are able to go.
Zakat does not apply if you are under the threshold.
There is no point where you finish the religion. You keep growing for the rest of your life.
focusNow: Learn the big picture of zakat and Hajj.
Stay close to teachers and a community you trust.
canWait: Working out detailed zakat sums without anyone reviewing your finances.
Planning Hajj before you can afford it and manage it physically.
Specializing in anything until you want to.
askHelpIf: You think zakat may now apply to you.
You are planning Hajj or Umrah.
You need guidance that touches money or law.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I live halal long term?
